svg.text: claudia composes — outline levels and numbered headings
Proposal for review — nothing is built (E9.22). A style has an outline level and may point at a list; the numbers are derived like list numbers, never typed.
A · Numbered headings in Flow view
The caret is in a Heading 2. Its number, 2.1, comes from the style: Heading 1 and 2 point at the list “Outline”, which uses the scheme “Chapters”.
Teachers asked for a way to show that a garden is worth the time it takes.
Fewer forms, and results they can show to parents.
Both schools kept their timetables; we only added a short survey.

text.tspan: first: the numbers depend on how we measured.

svg.text: The title has no outline level: it names the document,
so it is neither numbered nor in the table of contents.
Numbers hang in the margin, drawn from the heading style;
search, copy, the AI and the authorship view never see
them as characters (as list markers, E9.21).
A new heading numbers itself. Moving or deleting a section
renumbers everything after it, and a reference such as
Screen readers hear “heading level 2, 2.1 Two sites,
twelve weeks”: the outline level is the heading’s aria-level,
and its number is part of its accessible name.
Any style can be a heading: give it an outline level in
its editor (C). Nothing depends on the name “Heading”.
Two entries join the List flyout of E9.21. Number Headings is ticked while headings are numbered.
The caret is in a heading, not a list item, so the list entries that need an item are off.
Number Headings is one step in the history: every style with an outline level (Heading 1–6, and
any style of the person’s own) is pointed at the list “Outline” with the scheme “Chapters”.
Unticking takes the numbering off those styles again; the list stays, with its start number.
All Numbering… opens the numbering manager (D). Both are also in the native shells’ menus (D361).
C · The style editor gets an Outline section
Format ▸ Edit This Style… (Shift+F10) on the heading, and the same editor in All Styles. Only paragraph styles have it.

D · Format ▸ List ▸ All Numbering…: the numbering manager
All Styles’ twin: the schemes on the left, the chosen one on the right (D302). It edits the document’s schemes; lists and styles refer to them.
Levels 5–9 go on the same way ·
A change here renumbers them for everybody,
as one step in the history.
be changed and reset. The document carries its
schemes, so it looks the same on every server.
“Shows” is which levels the label carries: “levels 1–2”
draws 2.1; “this level” draws b. as the Numbers
scheme does. Number is 1 2 3, a b c, A B C, i ii iii,
I II III, a bullet, or nothing.
Used by names every list, style and paragraph a
change will touch; each name selects it.
A scheme in use cannot be deleted; the list that
uses it says why. A viewer sees the dialog read-only.
